input.quote: 28.1 This Agreement is governed exclusively by Singapore law, and the courts of Singapore have exclusive jurisdiction.
input.rationale: Section 28.1 selects Singapore law and exclusive Singapore courts, which is outside the accepted list (New York, Delaware, California, England and Wales) and approaches the walk-away position of a foreign exclusive venue. It also directly conflicts with Section 28.2, which vests exclusive jurisdiction in the state and federal courts in New York County. No arbitration clause appears in the document. The minimal fix changes only the jurisdiction words in 28.1 to New York law and conforms venue to the New York courts already named in 28.2, resolving the conflict and reaching the preferred position.

proposal.summary: Change governing law from Singapore to New York and conform venue to the New York courts named in Section 28.2
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have changed the governing law from Singapore to the State of New York and conformed the venue wording to the New York County courts already named in Section 28.2, since the two provisions otherwise conflict. Our playbook accepts New York (or, as a fallback, Delaware, California, or England and Wales with London courts), but not Singapore law or exclusive Singapore venue.

ops.oldText: Singapore law, and the courts of Singapore have exclusive jurisdiction.
ops.newText: the laws of the State of New York, excluding its conflict-of-laws rules, and the state and federal courts located in New York County, New York have exclusive jurisdiction as provided in Section 28.2.
